result: The authors generated a conditional knockout line for Dop1R2 using CRISPR-Cas9 with FRT sites. Immunohistochemistry shows HA-tag signal in the mushroom body (MB) of the Dop1R2cko line, which is abolished upon flippase-mediated excision using OK107-Gal4, demonstrating the efficiency of the flip-out system.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm the successful generation and validation of the genetic tool. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'design and implement an elegant strategy' with 'precise techniques for genetic perturbation.' Reviewer 2 notes the 'novel CRISPR/Cas9-based genetic tool' and that 'experiments impressively demonstrate the value of such a genetic tool.' Reviewer 4 emphasizes this is 'the most sophisticated approach to induce a loss of function phenotypes in neurons of interest.'

result: Dop1R2 is not required for short-term memory (STM) in any mushroom body lobe. Knockout of Dop1R2 in the whole MB, γ-lobe, α/β-lobes, or α'/β'-lobes does not affect aversive or appetitive STM. Control experiments show normal odor, sugar, and shock responses.
evaluation: Reviewers consistently accept these findings without challenge. Reviewer 1 states 'none of these manipulations affect short term appetitive or aversive memory.' Reviewer 2 notes 'dop1R2 is...dispensable for short-term memory.' Reviewer 3 confirms the findings show Dop1R2 is 'not required for short-term memory.' The experimental design is described as 'rigorous' with 'appropriately applied' statistics.

result: Dop1R2 is specifically required in the α/β-lobe and α'/β'-lobe but not in the γ-lobe for 2-hour memory (middle-term memory) after both aversive and appetitive training. Flip-out of Dop1R2 in these lobes impairs 2 hr memory performance.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm these findings. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'show that while none of these manipulations affect short term...memory, loss of dop1R2 from ab or a'b' block the ability of flies to display measurable forms of longer forms of memory.' Reviewer 3 notes the authors 'localize Dop1R2 function to the vertical lobes of the mushroom body, revealing a role in later (presumably middle-term) aversive and appetitive memory.' Reviewer 4 confirms 'dop1R2 is necessary in a/b and a'/b' but not in gamma neurons to display normal appetitive and aversive middle-term (2h)...memory.'

result: Dop1R2 is required in the α/β-lobes and α'/β'-lobes for long-term memory (LTM) at 24 hours after both aversive and appetitive training. No phenotype is observed when Dop1R2 is knocked out in the γ-lobe.
evaluation: Reviewers consistently support these LTM findings. Reviewer 1 states 'loss of dop1R2 from ab or a'b' block the ability of flies to display measurable forms of longer forms of memory,' which encompasses LTM. Reviewer 2 notes 'dop1R2 is necessary for longer lasting memories through its action on α/β and α'/β' neurons.' Reviewer 4 confirms 'dop1R2 is necessary in a/b and a'/b' but not in gamma neurons to display normal appetitive and aversive...long-term (24h) memory.' The conclusions are described as 'very well supported by the data.'

result: Pan-neuronal flip-out of Dop1R2 does not improve memory at 6 hr and 24 hr time points, confirming that Dop1R2 is irrelevant for memory outside the mushroom body.
evaluation: While not explicitly discussed by reviewers, this finding is presented as supporting data and is consistent with the reviewers' acceptance of the MB-specific localization of Dop1R2 function. Reviewer 4 notes the authors 'mapped these effects to two types of memory neurons in the fly brain,' implicitly accepting the specificity to MB neurons.

result: Post-eclosion temporal knockout experiments show that memory loss caused by Dop1R2 flip-out is not due to developmental defects. Anatomical organization of the MB is not altered, and the temporal knockout replicates the STM and LTM phenotypes.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about developmental effects, and Reviewer 3 notes the 'experimental design is rigorous.' The temporal control experiments strengthen the interpretation that Dop1R2 functions acutely in memory rather than through developmental effects, which reviewers implicitly accept by not questioning this aspect.

result: Single-cell transcriptomics analysis shows that Dop1R2 co-expresses more frequently with Gαo than with Gαq in mushroom body neurons.
evaluation: This finding is presented as supporting data for understanding Dop1R2 signaling mechanisms. Reviewers do not challenge this analysis, and it is consistent with the overall acceptance of the manuscript's findings about Dop1R2 function.

result: The Dop1R2cko genetic tool provides a sophisticated alternative to RNAi knockdowns and can be used in combination with Drosophila genetic tools to study dopamine receptor function with spatial and temporal precision.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly emphasize the value of the genetic tool. Reviewer 3 states 'The FRT lines generated provide a novel tool for temporal and spatially precise manipulation of Dop1R2 function. This tool will be valuable to study the role of Dop1R2 in memory and other behaviors.' Reviewer 4 notes 'the authors of this paper produced a tool to generate tissue-specific knock out mutants' and 'the genetic tools used here represent the most sophisticated approach to induce a loss of function phenotypes in neurons of interest.'
